judgment: On the sixth day, and only then, there is trust.
It is good to hold firm.
image: Fire inside the marsh: Change of Skin.
So the noble one sets the calendar in order
lines: When the sixth day comes, change it.
To march: misfortune. Holding firm: danger.
The talk of change is three times settled:
There is trust to change the charge.
The great person changes like a tiger.
Before the casting, there is trust.
The noble one changes like a leopard,
but the small person changes his face.

notes.name_en: 革 is hide/skin, and stripping a hide = change (tiger, leopard, face in L5-6); 'Change of Skin', not Wilhelm's 'Revolution (Moulting)'.
notes.judgment: 己日 the ji day (sixth stem-day) — rendered 'the sixth day' for consistency with 18 ('the first day', 甲) and 57 ('the seventh day', 庚); B adds 'only then' for 乃孚 (trust only on that day).
notes.L4: 改命 changing the charge/mandate; 命 as decree, not fate.
